where: my own method: a daemon started inside a systemd-run unit
what: The cold build ran as a `systemd-run` unit and its client started the daemon inside the unit's cgroup: when the unit's script ended systemd killed the daemon, so the next unit started a new one and timed a first build after a restart. A second time a client started while my daemon unit was not yet listening and spawned its own daemon, which waited 300 s on the first's lock.
cost: one 17 minute cold build measured for nothing; ten minutes
cause: the daemon is a child of whatever first asks for it
class: a measurement of another state than the one named
prevention: my scripts: the daemon is its own unit (`daemon.sh`, started first, the chain waits for its socket). For everyone: a how-to row
